housing: County Durham has a large stock of former colliery terraces in towns and villages such as Stanley, Horden, Easington and Ferryhill, many of them now privately rented and some long-term empty. Durham City has a big student market, with Victorian terraces turned into HMOs and purpose-built student blocks. Post-war new towns at Newton Aycliffe and Peterlee have planned estates, while Teesdale and Weardale in the west have stone cottages and farmhouses. House prices are among the lowest in England.
checkinTips: Colliery terraces in former mining villages: photograph back yards, outhouses, rear lanes and any damp in the back kitchen or on chimney breasts.
Former mining areas: note any cracks in walls and around frames so ground movement can be compared at check-out.
Student HMOs in Durham City: photograph each bedroom's lock and furniture, fire doors, alarms and every shared appliance separately.
Stone cottages in Teesdale and Weardale: check solid walls for damp, record the oil tank level, wood burners and any private water supply.
Coastal homes at Seaham: look for salt corrosion on metal frames, gates and outdoor fittings.
Long-empty terraces brought back into use: record the condition of every room in detail, including windows, doors and the boiler.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or unsafe conditions in a private rented home can contact Durham County Council's housing standards team, which can inspect and enforce standards.
